resources.title: Limits, L'Hopital's rule, and epsilon delta definitions | Chapter 7, Essence of calculus
resources.why_recommended: The clearest visual treatment of the epsilon-delta definition of a limit, the derivative as a limit, and L'Hopital's rule - the exact intuition GATE needs behind limit evaluation.

resources.title: MIT 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus (Fall 2010) - full course with recitations
resources.why_recommended: The self-paced MIT 18.01SC course opens with limits, continuity and differentiation from first principles, with lecture videos, worked recitations and problem sets - the gold standard for exam-level single-variable calculus.

resources.title: NPTEL Calculus of One Real Variable (IIT Kanpur)
resources.why_recommended: An IIT Kanpur NPTEL course that rigorously builds limits of functions, continuous functions, the Intermediate Value Theorem and differentiation - matching the theorem-driven depth expected in GATE.

resources.title: Paul's Online Math Notes - Calculus I: Limits
resources.why_recommended: Comprehensive free notes on computing limits, one-sided/infinite limits, continuity and L'Hospital's rule, each with worked examples and separate practice problem sets to drill the mechanics.

resources.title: Taylor series | Chapter 11, Essence of calculus
resources.why_recommended: The most intuitive explanation of how Taylor (and Maclaurin) polynomials approximate a function by matching successive derivatives at a point - it makes the factorial coefficients obvious.

resources.title: MIT 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus - Unit 5B: Taylor Series
resources.why_recommended: MIT 18.01SC has a dedicated Taylor Series unit (Unit 5, Part B) with lecture videos, notes and problem sets that derive Maclaurin expansions of e^x, sin x and cos x - directly examinable material.

resources.title: Paul's Online Math Notes - Calculus II: Taylor Series
resources.why_recommended: A clean, worked derivation of the Taylor and Maclaurin series formulas with the standard expansions (e^x, sin x, cos x) plus practice problems - ideal for building computational fluency for GATE.

topics.topic_name: Maxima and Minima (first- and second-derivative tests)

resources.title: MIT 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus - Unit 2B: Optimization, Related Rates and Newton's Method
resources.why_recommended: Covers critical points, the first- and second-derivative tests and concavity within MIT 18.01SC's applications unit, with recitation videos and problems that mirror GATE-style analysis.

resources.title: Paul's Online Math Notes - Calculus I: Minimum and Maximum Values
resources.why_recommended: Precisely distinguishes absolute vs relative extrema, states the Extreme Value Theorem and Fermat's Theorem, and links critical points to the first/second-derivative tests, with practice problems.

resources.title: Calculus 1 Lecture 2.4: Applications of the Derivative (increasing/decreasing, extrema)
resources.why_recommended: Professor Leonard's slow, worked-example lectures on applying the derivative to locate and classify maxima and minima using the first and second derivative tests are excellent for building confidence from scratch.

topics.topic_name: Single-Variable Optimization (incl. closed-interval / applied optimization, convexity intuition)

resources.title: Calculus 1 Lecture 3.7: Optimization; Max/Min Application Problems
resources.why_recommended: A thorough, step-by-step walkthrough of applied (word-problem) optimization: setting up the objective, using constraints, and finding the optimum - the exact skill GATE applied-optimization questions test.

resources.title: Paul's Online Math Notes - Calculus I: Optimization
resources.why_recommended: The definitive free notes on applied optimization, including the closed-interval method (checking critical points and endpoints), with many fully worked examples and practice problems.

resources.title: Khan Academy - Absolute minima & maxima (closed intervals) and Optimization
resources.why_recommended: Concise review plus free interactive practice on finding absolute extrema on a closed interval and solving optimization problems - a fast way to drill the endpoint-and-critical-point comparison method.

resources.title: MIT 18.01SC Single Variable Calculus - Unit 2B: Optimization
resources.why_recommended: MIT 18.01SC's optimization unit provides rigorous lecture videos and problem sets on setting up and solving single-variable optimization problems, reinforcing the applied techniques with exam-level rigor.
